How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, August 20, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Harrington
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF POLICE EXPLORER ISABELLA NAVARRO

  B. STREET PAVEMENT CONDITION INDEX

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of July 16, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of July 16, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  2
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JULY 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2024-2025 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for July 2024.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NOS. 24-46 AND 24-47 SETTING THE RATE
  AND AMOUNT NECESSARY FOR THE 2024-2025 FISCAL YEAR
  RETIREMENT LEVY

  The City’s retirement costs are funded by a special property tax levy authorized
  by the voters in 1948. The special property tax levy approved by the voters
  requires the City Council to annually establish a tax rate sufficient to meet the
  City’s obligations to the state employees’ retirement system. No change in the
  tax rate is recommended for the 2024-2025 fiscal year and the City Council is
  asked to confirm the current rate and fix the amount of property taxes to be
  generated by adopting two resolutions. Based on the assessed valuation
  ($7,167,766,644 – an increase of 5.3% over Fiscal Year 2023-2024 value)
  prepared by the Auditor Controller and the recommended continued levy of 14
  cents per $100 of assessed property value, the amount to be generated is
  estimated at $10,034,873 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025. This levy, along with the
  current fund balance in the Retirement Fund, will be sufficient to cover the
  retirement costs, budgeted at $10,838,690 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-46, setting the
  tax rate at 14 cents per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution No. 24-47,
  fixing the amount of property taxes to be generated for the City’s employees’
  retirement cost for fiscal year 2024-2025.

  E. APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT WITH LA CASA DE SAN GABRIEL
  COMMUNITY CENTER FOR THE DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $3,075

  The City has always partnered with a third-party entity to assist in obtaining an
  Alcohol Beverage Control (ABC) license for its annual Dumpling and Beer
  Festival. As the City does not have an exclusive partner for the event, every year
  presents an opportunity for the City to partner with a different entity. La Casa
  de San Gabriel Community Center was the only organization contacted by staff
  that expressed interest in partnering with the City to obtain the ABC license for
  the Festival. The cost for the City to contract with La Casa de San Gabriel
  Community Center to partner for the Dumpling and Beer Festival is $3,075 and
  has already been included in the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget under the
  Dumpling and Beer project line item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Agreement with La Casa
  de San Gabriel Community Center for the 2024 Dumpling and Beer festival and
  authorize the City Manager or their designee to execute said agreement.

  F. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH INDIGO CIVIL ENGINEERING
  INCORPORATED TO PROVIDE ENGINEERING AND DESIGN SERVICES FOR
  VINCENT LUGO PARK ACCESS PATH AND PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE
  REPLACEMENT PROJECT FOR $63,160 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  On April 20, 2023, the City of San Gabriel was awarded a grant through the Los
  Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District to improve the
  following: pedestrian access path from Vincent Lugo Park to the east end of an
  existing pedestrian bridge over the Alhambra Wash and onward to west end of

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  4
   Hovey Avenue; replace or reconstruct the existing worn-out pedestrian bridge
  over the Alhambra Wash; Install new handrails adjacent to the Alhambra Wash
  where there is only barbed wire currently; construct American Disabilities Act
  compliant ramping at the east end of the pedestrian bridge; and provide and
  install new wayfinding signs and path improvements The bridge restoration and
  path improvements will also enhance public safety. A Request for Proposal No.
  23-015 was advertised on the City’s website and staff has determined that
  Indigo Civil Engineering Incorporated is the best-suited firm to provide design
  and engineering services for the project. There is no fiscal impact to the General
  Fund. The adopted 2024-2025 Fiscal Year budget includes Measure A funds
  allocated for this project as outlined in Capital Improvement project No. 7-24-
  04 using budget account 122-800-57-97-908.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a Professional Services Agreement with Indigo Civil Engineering Incorporated
  and approve purchase orders for $69,456 which includes a 10% contingency.

  G. APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT WITH TAYLOR TENNIS COURTS,
  INCORPORATED IN THE AMOUNT OF $20,410 PLUS A $5,000
  CONTINGENCY FOR THE RESURFACING OF THE TENNIS COURTS AT
  ROOSEVELT ELEMENTARY SCHOOL AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO.
  24-28 FOR THE INCREASE OF APPROPRIATIONS IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $14,419 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-28]

  In April 2024, the two tennis courts at Smith Park were converted to one
  permanent pickleball court and one multi-use court for pickleball and tennis
  players. In order to accommodate the reduction of tennis courts, the City
  decided to reopen Roosevelt Elementary School tennis courts to serve the
  tennis players. However, the existing courts haven’t been resurfaced in more
  than 20 years and are in need of resurfacing before reopening to the public.
  Should the City Council approve the resurfacing and restriping project at
  Roosevelt Elementary School, an additional $14,419 in funding would need to
  be allocated from the general fund to the special project fund, 124-850-18-96-
  816. There is currently $10,991 in this fund that will carry over from Fiscal Year
  2023-2024. The fund was initially developed to complete the tennis/pickleball
  court resurfacing and restriping project at Smith Park which has since been
  completed.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  5
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  project as defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines, as resurfacing
  of existing tennis courts at Roosevelt Elementary School does not reasonably
  create a possibility that the work will have any significant affect to the
  environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a contract with Taylor Tennis Courts, Incorporated in the amount of $20,410
  plus a contingency for $5,000 using account number 124-850-18-96-816.
  Additionally, staff recommends the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-28 to
  increase appropriations to the special project fund in the amount of $14,419.

  H. AMENDMENT AGREEMENT (OPTION 2) WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY FOR
  CATCH BASIN MAINTENANCE WITH NEGLIGIBLE FISCAL IMPACT

  The City of San Gabriel is required to install and maintain trash capture devices
  on storm drain catch basins to reduce debris entering the Los Angeles River
  through stormwater discharge. An amendment of the Agreement (Option 2)
  with the Los Angeles County Flood Control District is requested as one
  additional catch basin will be installed, one existing but unincluded catch basin
  will be accounted for, and three catch basins will be modified during the
  Broadway and Walnut Grove Avenue Intersection Project with negligible fiscal
  impact for maintaining one additional catch basin. City staff will bill the Los
  Angeles County Flood Control District per the current Catch Basin Cleanout
  Cost schedule, including an annual Consumer Price Index rate and as specified
  in the Option 2 Agreement. Adding two additional catch basins and modifying
  three existing catch basins will have an insignificant cost impact.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  an amendment to the Agreement (Option 2) with the Los Angeles County Flood
  Control District for catch basin maintenance.

  I. AWARD AGREEMENT TO ATHENS SERVICES FOR ADDITIONAL BULKY
  ITEM COLLECTION SUPPORT IN THE AMOUNT OF $88,750

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  6
   For many years, the City has partnered with Athens Services to provide street
  sweeping and solid waste collection services. The existing agreement allows
  residents to request two free bulky item pick-ups each week by notifying
  Athens Services. Unfortunately, illegal dumping remains a chronic problem,
  creating a significant amount of work several times a week for Public Works
  staff. By receiving additional support from Athens Services, Public Works field
  staff can focus on more critical tasks throughout the City. The adopted budget
  for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 included funding for additional Bulky Item Collection
  Support from the Solid Waste budget account 124-800-55-96-514.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  an agreement with Athens Services for additional Bulky Item Collection support
  (Option 2 of the proposal) and approve a purchase order with Athens Services
  for $88,750.

  J. MUNICIPAL PROGRAM TRANSFER AGREEMENT WITH THE SAFE, CLEAN
  WATER PROGRAM (MEASURE W) FUNDING

  In order to receive approximately $445,000 from the voter-approved Safe,
  Clean Water Program (Measure W), the City and the Los Angeles County Flood
  Control District must execute a Municipal Transfer Agreement. This Agreement
  will enable the City to receive annual funding for Citywide Stormwater Capital
  Improvement Projects, Water Quality Improvement Projects, Stormwater and
  Urban Runoff Capture Projects, City staff labor for construction projects and
  administrative tasks related to the Program. The funds that will be transferred
  from the City via the Transfer Agreement are currently estimated at
  approximately $445,000 annually. Funds have been budgeted under the
  Stormwater Fund 138 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-44 and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the Transfer Agreement between the
  City, and the Los Angeles Flood Control District to receive Safe, Clean Water
  Program (Measure W) funding.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  7
   K. AWARD CONTRACT NO. 24-02 TO SULLY-MILLER CONTRACTING
  COMPANY FOR THE WALNUT GROVE AVENUE AND BROADWAY
  INTERSECTION IMPROVEMENT PROJECT, CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECT NO. 1-08-11 FOR $2,172,641 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  The Walnut Grove Avenue and Broadway Intersection Improvement Project,
  Capital Improvement Project No. 1-08-11 will consist of widening the
  intersection, upgrading traffic signals, improving sidewalk and parkway
  conditions, and reconstructing the pavement in the intersection and its
  approaches. This intersection is identified as a poor-performing intersection in
  the General Plan, and its proximity to three schools adds significant traffic and
  pedestrian volumes during peak weekday periods. The project will improve the
  level of service, congestion, pollution, traffic flow, and safety. Sully-Miller
  Contracting Company was the lowest responsive bidder. The adopted Fiscal
  Year 2024-2025 budget includes a construction funding of $990,625 in various
  accounts. The original Engineer Cost Estimate was about $850,000, 14 years
  ago. Materials and construction costs have increased dramatically throughout
  the years, especially after the pandemic. Staff is requesting an appropriation of
  $1,399,281 from the Measure M Fund to account 122-800-59-97-706 for the
  construction of the project plus a 10% contingency. This project will be
  managed and inspected using in-house staff.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to be Categorically Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – Existing
  Facilities. The project will improve the existing condition of the intersections. No
  potential significant impacts to the environment are anticipated in this project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-40 to appropriate an additional $1,399,281 from
  the Measure M fund account 122-800-59-97-706;
  2. Approve plans and specifications for the Walnut Grove and Broadway
  Intersection Improvement Project;

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute Contract No. 24-02 with Sully-Miller
  Contracting; and
  4. Approve a purchase order for $2,172,641 and a purchase order for a 10%
  construction contingency.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  8
   L. ONE-YEAR RENEWAL OF CENTRAL SQUARE PERMITTING SOFTWARE
  CONTRACT IN THE AMOUNT OF $30,334.49

  The Central Square permitting software has been integral to the efficient
  operation of the Community Development Department, providing efficient
  processes for permit applications, reviews, and approvals. Given the software’s
  critical role in the department’s operations, it is necessary to ensure its
  continued availability and functionality through the renewal of the current
  contract. The cost of the contract renewal, $30,334.49, is budgeted within the
  Community Development Department’s annual operating budget. There is no
  additional financial impact or budget adjustment required.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the renewal of the Central
  Square permitting software contract for one year at a cost of $30,334.49 and
  authorize the City Manager or his designee to sign the agreement.

  M. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-45 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED
  SCHEDULE OF COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS FOR REGULAR NON-
  REPRESENTED EMPLOYEES, ADJUSTING THE BASE SALARY AND HEALTH
  BENEFIT CONTRIBUTION FOR CITY MANAGER IN ACCORDANCE WITH
  THE CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT, ADJUSTING THE
  HEALTH BENEFIT CONTRIBUTION FOR CITY COUNCILMEMBERS IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE 53208.5, AND INCREASING
  BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR INCREASED SALARIES AND BENEFITS

  In June, staff began meeting with the Focus Group to discuss the status of the
  Authorized Schedule of Compensation and Benefits (ASCB) for regular non-
  represented employees. Representatives of the City and the Focus Group have
  mutually agreed upon a successor ASCB for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 presented in
  this staff report. The amended ASCB for the City’s regular non-represented
  employees is expected to have an annualized cost impact of $664,081. The
  increase is spread over multiple departments and funds, with the General Fund
  incurring $496,216 (74.7%), Retirement Fund incurring $48,243 (7.3%) and other
  funds incurring $119,622 (18.0%) of the total $664,081. An additional
  appropriation of $496,216 in General Funds, $48,243 in Retirement Funds, and
  $119,622 in other funds is needed to cover the increased cost of the amended
  ASCB for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  9
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-45, which
  amends and approves the Authorized Schedule of Compensation and Benefits
  for the City’s non-represented employees for Fiscal Year 2024-2025, effectuates
  a contractual adjustment to the base salary and maximum health benefit
  contribution provided to the City Manager, effectuates a statutory adjustment
  to the maximum health benefit contribution provided to City Councilmembers,
  and increase General Fund appropriations $496,216, Retirement Fund
  appropriations $48,243, and various other benefits appropriations $119,622 to
  cover increased costs to salaries and benefits for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  N. THEATRE FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY ASSEMBLYMEMBER MIKE FONG FOR
  PET WELLNESS DAY EVENT

  Assemblymember Mike Fong has requested a waiver of rental fees for the 49 th
  District’s upcoming Pet Wellness Day event, scheduled to take place on October
  19, 2024 in the Mission Playhouse parking lot. The request is for a fee waiver of
  their rental cost of $2,453 to reduce their cost to $0. If the other traditionally-
  offered events take place in the 2024/2025 year, granting the recommended
  fee waiver for this event would put the #152-3532 account into a $318 deficit
  at the end of Fiscal Year 2024-2025. As the other events also request a waiver,
  staff, if needed, will bring the request for additional funding forward at that
  time.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve a full waiver of the Mission
  Playhouse rental fee in the amount of $2,453 for the October 19, 2024 Pet
  Wellness Day Event.

  O. APPROVAL OF A THREE-YEAR SUBSCRIPTION TO MICROSOFT OFFICE 365
  FOR THE POLICE DEPARTMENT IN AN ANNUAL AMOUNT OF $23,232.52

  In August 2021, for the Police Department, City implemented Office 365. Office
  365 offers applications such as Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint,
  among others. These tools have facilitated seamless communication, document

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  10
   management, and collaboration across departments. The remainder of the
  City’s Office 365 users are under a different subscription agreement. The
  proposed costs for the Police Department’s Microsoft Office 365 subscription
  is $23,232.52 per year, effective through August 2025. The payment is on a year-
  to-year basis. Funds have been appropriated in the Fiscal Year 2024-2025
  Information Technology Internal Service Fund for this purchase.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a three-year subscription agreement with Microsoft Office 365 for the
  City’s Police Department in an amount not to exceed $69,697.56.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. 607 WEST ROSES ROAD – PLANNING CASE NO: GPA21-001, ZC21-001,
  ZTA21-001, AND LTLA21-009 (GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT, ZONE
  CHANGE, ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT, AND LOT LINE ADJUSTMENT) –
  APPLICANT: SAN GABRIEL CEMETERY [ORDINANCE NO. 711 –
  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING] + [RESOLUTION NO. 24-43]

  The subject request is a General Plan Amendment (GPA), Zone Change (ZC),
  Zone Text Amendment (ZTA), and Lot Line Adjustment (LTLA) to expand a
  cemetery use at 607 West Roses Road. The property is located in the R-1
  (Single-Family Residence) Zone and has a General Plan Land Use designation
  of Low Density Residential. The Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Adopted Budget includes
  the cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and
  codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance, if adopted by
  the City Council.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: According to the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and CEQA Guidelines, discretionary
  projects are subject to environmental review. Following preliminary review, an
  initial study was prepared to determine if the project may have a significant effect
  on the environment. The initial study showed that the project would potentially
  cause a substantial adverse change in the significance of a historical resource as
  defined in Public Resources Code Section 21084.1 and CEQA Guidelines Section
  15064.5.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  11
   Pursuant to the provisions of the CEQA Guidelines, the City circulated a Notice of
  Preparation (NOP) to State, regional, County, and local agencies; Native
  American Tribes, and interested members of the public. The NOP was made
  available for public review at multiple locations, including the San Gabriel Public
  Library and City Hall. The NOP public comment period began on August 24, 2023,
  and concluded on September 22, 2023, providing a 31-day comment period. The
  purpose of the NOP was to formally convey that the City was preparing a Draft
  Environmental Impact Report (DEIR) for the proposed project, and to solicit input
  regarding the scope and content of the environmental information to be included
  in the Draft EIR.

  The Draft EIR was circulated for a 45-day public review period between April 16,
  2024 and May 30, 2024, in compliance with CEQA Guidelines. A notice regarding
  the public review period was posted with the Los Angeles County Recorder,
  published in the San Gabriel Sun newspaper, and distributed to relevant
  regulatory agencies. Additionally, a notice was mailed to organizations or
  individuals who had previously requested notice or expressed an interest in the
  project.

  During the Draft EIR public review period, the City reviewed one comment letter
  from agencies and organizations through written correspondence and emails.
  Following the close of the public review period, the City prepared a Final EIR,
  which includes responses to comments received on the Draft EIR. In addition, a
  Mitigation Montoring and Reporting Program (MMRP) is included in the Final EIR
  to ensure the mitigation measures identified in the EIR are implemented, thereby
  minimizing the identified environmental effects.

  Recommended Action:

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the General Plan Amendment, Zone Change, Zone Text Amendment,
  and Lot Line Adjustment applications. Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-43 certifying the Final Environmental Impact
  Report, making findings required by the California Environmental Quality
  Act and adopting a Statement of Overriding Considerations and Mitigation
  Monitoring and Reporting Program, and approving the project located at
  607 West Roses Road;

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 711 by title only, and waive
  future reading; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  12
   3. Schedule the Second Reading and adoption of the Ordinance for the next
  regular City Council meeting. The Second Reading will require a majority
  vote of the total membership of the City Council.

  Alternative Option for Consideration:

  Option 1: Should the City Council determine that the proposed project or any
  part of the proposed project should be denied, the Council should deliberate
  and provide the required findings, direct staff to return with a Resolution for
  the DENIAL of Planning Case Nos. GPA21-001, ZC21-001, ZTA22-001 and
  LTLA21-009 at the regularly-scheduled City Council Meeting of September 17,
  2024.

  Option 2: The City Council could also discuss the proposed project and suggest
  changes that would allow the project to be approved with modifications.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 713 AMENDING TITLE III, SECTION 34 OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE – FINANCE AND REVENUE –
  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  The proposed ordinance would amend Title III, Section 34 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code. The ordinance would amend, in part, the dollar thresholds
  required for formal and informal contract procedures as well as the City
  Manager authority to make purchases, increasing the amounts from
  $15,000 to $25,000. The ordinance would also amend the amount required
  to obtain three informal written bids from $3,000 to $5,000 and propose
  some minor text changes. There is no fiscal impact for this item. However,
  operational efficiencies may be achieved due to higher thresholds for when
  bids are required and when purchases are required to be taken to the City
  Council for approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and introduce by title
  only Ordinance No. 713 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the
  City of San Gabriel, California, Amending Chapter 34 of the San Gabriel

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  13
   Municipal Code Regarding Formal Contract Procedures, Open Market
  Procedures, Professional and Specialized Services, Purchase of Used
  Equipment, Award of Contracts, and Disposition of Obsolete and Surplus
  Equipment;” waive future reading; and schedule the second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance for the next regularly-scheduled City Council
  meeting.

  Alternative Recommendations:

  A) Propose Different Amounts: Staff is recommending increasing the ‘no
  bid’ limit up to $5,000 and the City Manager’s purchasing authority up
  to $25,000. As an alternative recommendation, the City Council may
  propose different amounts for the no bid limit and/or the City Manager’s
  purchasing authority.

  B) Propose No Changes Be Made: There is no requirement to make
  changes to the City’s purchasing policy. Therefore, the City Council may
  propose to maintain the status quo and not make any changes to the
  City purchasing policy.

  B. GRANT-WRITING SERVICES UPDATE

  On January 16, 2024, the City of San Gabriel entered into a Professional
  Services Agreement with California Consulting, Incorporated (Consultant)
  for grant-writing services. The purpose of hiring the Consultant is to assist
  the City apply for various state and federal grant funding opportunities that
  would benefit all departments. This report is to provide the City Council with
  an overview of the completed and future grant applications. The Fiscal Year
  2023-2024 general fund non-departmental budget included $50,000 for
  grant writing services. The annual proposed cost of the agreement was
  $55,200. The annualized cost was prorated based on a mid-January start
  date with an estimated cost of $25,300, which resulted in budget savings.
  For Fiscal Year 2024-2025, the agreement is budgeted at the full contract
  agreement rate of $4,600 per month or $55,200 annually.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  This is an information item only. No action is required.

  C. DISCUSSION REGARDING THE FARMERS MARKET

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 20, 2024  14
   In late April, the City and Supporting Arms launched the San Gabriel Farmers
  Market. The Farmers Market was located at the Park and Ride lot on Mission
  Drive and included 2-3 produce vendors, 6-7 artisan makers, and at least 4
  hot food vendors. The market also included live music, fun kid activities and
  interactive activities with the Police Department, Fire Department, and
  Public Works Department. In addition to the activities, City Staff advertised
  the event via a mailer to the surrounding properties, street and pedestrian
  signage, a month-long tote giveaway, and paid social media ads. Despite
  these efforts, the Farmers Market was not able to consistently retain the
  vendors and attendance to the event decreased. There is no fiscal impact as
  a result of this project.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the Farmers Market event
  and provide direction to staff regarding a new location, day, and time for
  the Farmers Market.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The City Council will adjourn the meeting in honor and memory of Rosita H.
  Lugo, a 102-year resident of San Gabriel. Rosita dedicated and served the
  community for decades by volunteering and contributing to numerous
  community service events.

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, September 17,
  2024 at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:30 P.M.
  on Tuesday, August 20, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Harrington.

  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.

  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

  and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Wu approved the agenda order.

  Certificate of Recognition.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

I  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of July 16, 2024.

  The City Council approved July 3, 5, 11, 19, and 29, 2024, Material Demands for the

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 7  August 20, 2024
   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT- JULY 2024

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for July 2024.

  D. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NOS. 24-46 AND 24-47 SETTING THE RATE AND
  AMOUNT NECESSARY FOR THE 2024-2025 FISCAL VEAR RETIREMENT LEVY

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-46, setting the tax rate at 14 cents
  per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution No. 24-47, fixing the amount of

I  property taxes to be generated for the City's employees' retirement cost for fiscal
  year 2024-2025.

  E. APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT WITH LA CASA DE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY
  CENTER FOR THE DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $3,075

  The City Council approved the Agreement with La Casa de San Gabriel Community

  INCORPORATED TO PROVIDE ENGINEERING AND DESIGN SERVICES FOR
  VINCENT LUGO PARK ACCESS PATH AND PEDESTRIAN BRIDGE
  REPLACEMENT PROJECT FOR $63,160 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute a Professional Services

  orders for $69,456 which includes a 10% contingency.

  CATCH BASIN MAINTENANCE WITH NEGLIGIBLE FISCAL IMPACT

I  Agreement (Option 2) with the Los Angeles County Flood Control District for catch

  COLLECTION SUPPORT IN THE AMOUNT OF $88,750

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 7  August 20, 2024

  FOR $2,172,641 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY

  The City Council:

  2. Approved plans and specifications for the Walnut Grove and Broadway
  Intersection Improvement Project;

  3. Authorized the City Manager to execute Contract No. 24-02 with Sully-Miller
  Contracting; and

  4. Approved a purchase order for $2,172,641 and a purchase order for a 10%
  construction contingency.

  L. ONE-VEAR RENEWAL OF CENTRAL SQUARE PERMITTING  SOFTWARE
  CONTRACT IN THE AMOUNT OF $30,334.49

  The City Council approved the renewal of the Central Square permitting software

I  contract for one year at a cost of $30,334.49 and authorized the City Manager or

  M. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-45 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED
  SCHEDULE OF COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS FOR REGULAR NON-
  REPRESENTED EMPLOYEES, ADJUSTING THE BASE SALARY AND HEALTH
  BENEFIT CONTRIBUTION FOR CITY MANAGER IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE

  BENEFIT CONTRIBUTION FOR CITY COUNCILMEMBERS IN ACCORDANCE
  WITH GOVERNMENT CODE 53208.5, AND INCREASING BUDGET
  APPROPRIATIONS FOR INCREASED SALARIES AND BENEFITS

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-45, which amends and approves the
  Authorized Schedule of Compensation and Benefits for the City's non-represented
  employees for Fiscal Year 2024-2025, effectuates a contractual adjustment to the
  base salary and maximum health benefit contribution provided to the City
  Manager, effectuates a statutory adjustment to the maximum health benefit
  contribution provided to City Councilmembers, and increases General Fund

I  appropriations $496,216, Retirement Fund appropriations $48,243, and various
  other benefits appropriations $119,622 to cover increased costs to salaries and
  benefits for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  N. THEATRE FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY ASSEMBLVMEMBER MIKE FONG FOR PET
  WELLNESS DAV EVENT
  The City Council approved a full waiver of the Mission Playhouse rental fee in the
  amount of $2,453 for the October 19, 2024, Pet Wellness Day Event.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 7  August 20, 2024
   0. APPROVAL OF A THREE-VEAR SUBSCRIPTION TO MICROSOFT OFFICE 365
  FOR THE POLICE DEPARTMENT IN AN ANNUAL AMOUNT OF $23,232.52

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to enter into a three-year
  subscription agreement with Microsoft Office 365 for the City's Police Department
  in an amount not to exceed $69,697.56.

  CHANGE, ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT, AND LOT LINE ADJUSTMENT) -
  APPLICANT: SAN GABRIEL CEMETERY [ORDINANCE NO. 711 -
  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING] + [RESOLUTION NO. 24-43]

  Mayor Wu opened the public hearing.

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart made the staff presentation and San Gabriel
  Cemetery Board President John Babcock made the applicant presentation.

  The following provided written comments in support of the project: Ira (Mike)
  Matthiessen, resident; Mershie Shaw, resident; Lynn Snowden, resident; and Laurie
  Wheeler, resident.

  Mayor Wu closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included the project's benefit to the community.

I  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Harrington, to:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-43 certifying the Final Environmental Impact Report,
  making findings required by the California Environmental Quality Act and
  adopting a Statement of Overriding Considerations and Mitigation Monitoring
  and Reporting Program, and approving the project located at 607 West Roses
  Road;

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 711 by title only, and waive
  future reading; and

  3. Schedule the Second Reading and adoption of the Ordinance for the next
  regular City Council meeting.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

I  ABSENT:  NONE

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

  B. GRANT-WRITING SERVICES UPDATE

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included appreciation for the grant applications that have been made;
  application process management; the possibility of a grant for Smith Park pool
  renovation; coordination between City staff and the consultant for grants found by
  staff independently; eligibility criteria is specific for each grant; and challenges

  C. DISCUSSION REGARDING THE FARMERS MARKET

  Community Development Director Cervantes made the presentation.

  Erlinda Romo, resident, commented that more than two fresh food vendors are

I  types of vendors and products; fees; consultant agreement wording; seating for
  customers; being pet and family-friendly; current number of street food vendors in

   Council Member Chan commented on the City's National Night Out event and
